title: Anyone with a free Google account can park about 1 GB on our server through the workout copy
what: Signing in with Google is open to everyone, gym or not. The saved copy of workouts takes up to 30,000 pieces of up to 32 KB each per account, about 1 GB, at 200 pieces a call with no daily cap. A few throwaway Google accounts and a small script could fill the shared database that every gym uses, or run up the storage bill.
expected: A cap that fits real use: a member's real copy is a few MB, so a much smaller per-account size, a daily write budget, and a warning to us when one account grows fast.
fix_line: Lower the per-account size to what a heavy real member uses, add a daily write limit, and alert on fast growth

title: When the coach comes back, words a trainer types into a gym plan could steer it into deleting a member's workouts
what: The coach is switched off today. When on, it reads the member's routines, and plans sent by the gym land there with the trainer's own names and words. Those words reach the AI mixed in with the member's data, not marked as untrusted. Deleting a workout, meal or routine is stopped only by a sentence asking the AI to confirm first; the app itself never asks the member. A plan named like an order to the AI could make it delete data.
expected: The app, not the AI, asks the member to confirm every delete, and text from the gym or a backup is passed to the AI clearly marked as data, never as instructions.
who: members (only once the coach is switched on)
fix_line: Before switching the coach on, make deletes wait for a Yes button in the app and fence gym-sent text as data

title: When MettleUp Plus limits go live, restoring a backup gets around the 7 own exercises limit
what: The limit on own exercises is only checked when the member makes one in the exercise form. Restoring a backup file (anyone's, edited or not) brings in any number of own exercises with no check, and the check lets everything through on any error. The gate is off today, so nothing is lost yet.
expected: Decide on purpose: either restoring is allowed to carry any number (say so in the plan rules) or the restore keeps the extra ones read-only until Plus.
who: us (lost Plus sales), once the gate is on
fix_line: Write down whether a restore may go over the free limit, and check it there too if not
